title: Developer Rapid-Adopt Messaging & Pricing Playdraft
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playdraft for short-form developer-focused messaging that emphasizes fast time-to-value, predictable economics, and low operational lift. Target is engineers and ML builders evaluating a hosted inference API for production features (chat, generation, embeddings).

Tone & Voice:
- Direct, pragmatic, engineer-first.
- Emphasize measurable outcomes (latency, cost per token, integration time).
- Avoid marketing fluff; use concrete examples and playbook-style steps.

One-line value hypothesis:
- "Ship LLM features in hours, not months: consistent latency & transparent unit economics for production apps."

Key selling pillars (developer framing):
1) Fast integration: tiny SDK, single API key, sample app that runs locally in <10 minutes.
2) Predictable performance: per-route SLAs, latency percentiles surfaced in-console.
3) Cost clarity: per-token meter with recommended batching/caching profiles and an easy cost-estimate tool.
4) Safe fallbacks: built-in model variants and auto-fallback policies to avoid outages.

Quickstart angles (what to emphasize in first 2 screens of a quickstart):
- "Run the demo locally" (clone + npm start) -> see a chat UI talking to an OpenModel in <10 minutes.
- Show the exact curl/SDK call + expected response size so devs can immediately measure latency and tokens.
- Include a one-click toggle to simulate production throughput and see cost estimates.

Pricing-language drafts (short snippets for UI / emails):
- "Pay only for what you use — per-token billing with transparent cost breakdowns per model/route."
- "Reserved capacity for consistent throughput — commit to a baseline to lower unit price and unlock priority routing."
- "Estimate your bill in seconds: paste 3 prompts and we’ll show monthly cost at X rps."
- "Free tier for devs: 20k tokens/month + sample app templates; upgrade when you hit production traffic."

Microcopy and CTA options (for quickstart and sign-up flow):
- "Get an API key — start a local demo"
- "Run the sample chat in 2 minutes"
- "Estimate my monthly cost"
- "Reserve capacity (teams)"

Competitive framing notes (short):
- OpenAI-style incumbents: simplicity & model freshness are advantages — counter with "predictable SLOs and cost profiles" and developer controls (batching/caching presets).
- Cloud managed endpoints: they offer infra familiarity but often lack LLM-specific runtime optimizations — call out Redwood's inference optimizations and model variants for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Self-hosted runtimes / inference vendors: developers who want control build this themselves; emphasize "ship faster, operate less" and provide migration tooling (export configs, infra templates).

Objection handling (developer objections):
- "We already use X model elsewhere": offer side-by-side perf/cost snapshots and a migration checklist.
- "We can self-host for cheaper": show total cost of ownership for first 12 months including engineering time and incident overhead.
- "Can we trust latency at scale?": share percentile-based latency charts, SLA language, and a link to a reproducible load test.

Subject lines & short leads for outreach (A/B variants):
- "Try a chat demo in 5 minutes — see latency & cost"
- "Cut per-token cost with smart batching — quick calculator inside"
- "Reserve predictable throughput for your LLM features"

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Test A: Quickstart that emphasizes time-to-first-response (demo in 5m) vs Test B: Quickstart emphasizing cost transparency (estimate tool first).
- Test metrics: sign-up -> key generation, demo-run completion, estimated cost clicks, 7-day retention, first paid conversion.

Content components for the quickstart page (ordered):
1) One-line promise + single CTA (Get API key)
2) Inline 3-step guide (1. create key, 2. run sample, 3. view performance) with code snippets
3) Live latency & tokens example (pre-baked prompt)
4) Cost estimator widget next to the sample
5) "How it compares" strip showing expected latency/cost vs 2 competitors (numbers only)
6) Link to migration checklist and dedicated capacity info for teams

Customer-facing pricing blurbs (longer form for docs/FAQ):
- "Hosted API: Pay-as-you-go at listed per-token rates. Ideal for experimentation and variable workloads.
  Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit pricing, billed monthly.
  Private: For regulated workloads; contact sales for license and hosting options."

Guidelines for copy length by placement:
- Banner / hero: 6–12 words.
- Quickstart step titles: 2–4 words.
- Inline benefit bullets: 6–12 words each.
- Email first line: 20–35 words (problem -> quick win -> CTA).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- How big should the dev free tier be to drive activation but avoid abuse? (20k v 50k v 100k tokens)
- Do we gate the cost estimator behind account creation? My recommendation: allow it publicly but nudge sign-up for precise estimates.
- Do we surface a simple TCO calculator vs direct competitor prices in the quickstart? Needs legal sign-off on comparative claims.

Research & data needed to finalize:
- Benchmark table: 3 common prompt sizes, latency p50/p95, and per-token cost across top 3 model choices.
- Real onboarding funnel data: how long does it actually take new dev to run sample app? instrument code.
- Abuse / fraud historical rates to size free tier.

Appendix (workshop notes):
- Workshop idea: 45-minute session with 4 engineers building the sample chat from scratch; timebox each step and observe friction.
- Quick wins: add an "estimate cost" link to the hero, and show sample SDK code with a single copy-paste block.

This doc is intentionally compact — use it as a source for 1) hero copy, 2) quickstart flow, 3) pricing snippets to test in the next two weeks.
action_items: Instrument quickstart sample to capture time-to-first-response metrics
Add cost estimator widget to quickstart page (public) and track sign-ups
Draft legal-friendly competitor comparison language and route for sign-off
Run 2 developer sessions to validate friction and free tier sizing

Estimate your monthly LLM cost in 30s
Ship chat features faster — quickstart + cost calc
microcopy_snippets: Get an API key — start a local demo
Run the sample chat in 2 minutes
pricing_blurbs: Pay-as-you-go: per-token billing with transparent breakdowns
Reserved capacity: commit monthly to lower unit price and unlock priority routing
Private deployments: contact sales for pricing and compliance options
experiment_notes: Primary A/B: time-to-demo vs cost-first quickstart. Secondary: CTA wording ("Run demo" vs "Estimate cost"). Key success metric: demo completion rate and 7-day active usage.
competitor_notes: Call out three competitor patterns: 1) simplicity-first incumbents (fast dev loop but opaque cost), 2) cloud endpoint providers (familiar infra but generic runtimes), 3) self-hosted stacks (control but high ops). Position Redwood as the bridge: developer speed + production economics.
